explanation:
Streams are in-order queues; separate streams may overlap. Pageable copies go through a staging buffer and are
effectively synchronous. Events are the way to express cross-stream dependencies. Streams only help when there is
independent work and free resources; a kernel that fills the GPU leaves nothing to overlap with. The legacy default
stream synchronizes with other blocking streams (compile with `--default-stream per-thread` or use non-blocking
streams to avoid it).
